text:
Raj (Account Exec): FinEdge confirmed they'd like Redwood to be a drop-in replacement for CompetitorX. Key must-haves: identical response shape, x-api-key header present, same 4xx/5xx formats, and webhook callbacks for async job updates. Their POC window: 3 weeks with an initial smoke in 10 business days.
Maya (Solutions Eng): got it. do we have their OpenAPI file + a corpus of sample requests? need to map: streaming SSE vs polling webhooks, and whether request_id must be preserved.
Raj (Account Exec): they uploaded the spec to our shared drive. I'll DM the link. they use a top-level "id" field and sometimes include "trace.context" in responses.
Oliver (SRE): for POC infra, recommend ephemeral staging pool: 3x T4 equiv to start, escalate to 6 on autoscale. will create staging allowlist and temp credentials. ops-bot: ticket INF-4910 created for staging cluster.
Maya (Solutions Eng): we can implement a small proxy shim in the gateway that rewrites request/response JSON keys. plan: accept x-api-key as-is, forward to Redwood auth, then remap response to include their id/trace keys. simple rule-based mapper.
Tina (Security): they want explicit answers on payload retention and whether request bodies are stored in plaintext. sec-bot: added questionnaire link -> https://redwood.internal/sec/q/finedge-poc.json :lock:
Tina (Security): POC ok with our staging KMS, but prod expects customer-managed KMS + audit logs. note: customer will ask for encryption-at-rest confirmation.
Raj (Account Exec): pricing question: they bill per request + per-token. need a delta vs CompetitorX. can we run a token-delta on representative set?
Maya (Solutions Eng): yes — will run 60 sample prompts through both systems and report token counts + sample responses for parity diffs. will also record header outputs we must keep (X-Request-ID, X-Token-Usage).
Oliver (SRE): performance target: they will hit steady 150 rps with 600 concurrent long-poll callbacks. confirm whether staging pool can mimic that burst.
Maya (Solutions Eng): for POC we'll scope to synchronous generate endpoint first (no streaming). streaming SSE parity is a separate engineering spike. that keeps timeline realistic.
Raj (Account Exec): they require exact error bodies for 429 and 401 for their client library to not break. can the proxy map Redwood error shapes to CompetitorX shapes?
Maya (Solutions Eng): yes. implement an error_map table: common Redwood codes -> competitor-shaped JSON with identical fields. we'll also preserve HTTP status codes unless they insist otherwise.
Oliver (SRE): blockers: IP allowlist from client, CORS/webhook endpoint verification flow, and certificate pinning on their side. need those before end-to-end tests.
Tina (Security): also confirm data delete flows for POC: they asked whether requests can be purged on demand. we can support deletion from staging but must log it.
Raj (Account Exec): acceptance tests they will run: 1) identical JSON key presence for 20 canonical calls, 2) same error body for induced 429, 3) token accounting matches within 2%.
Maya (Solutions Eng): action items: - Raj to share OpenAPI + 60 samples (Raj) - ops-bot to provision INF-4910 (Oliver) - Maya to build shim and run parity tests (Maya) - Tina to start SOC2/KMS answers and track questionnaire (Tina)
Oliver (SRE): created ephemeral host staging-redwood-finedge, creds stored in vault. will post bench numbers once warm.
Maya (Solutions Eng): quick note: if they insist on exact timestamps (e.g., server_time), we can inject a server_time field but it will differ from competitor by a few ms. flag this in acceptance criteria.
Raj (Account Exec): I'll confirm acceptance criteria with FinEdge and loop back. thanks all. :thumbsup:
